# Nebraska Animal Medical Center

# Chemotherapy

We know it can be difficult to discover that your pet has cancer. We’re here to help you every step of the way from diagnosis to treatment.

Image: Woman with Dog on Bench

### We will partner with you to help your animal friend fight.

If your pet has been diagnosed with cancer, it can be devastating news. Nebraska Animal Medical And Emergency Center will partner with you to help your animal friend fight this illness. We offer pet chemotherapy in Lincoln and will do everything we can to keep your beloved companion by your side as long as possible.

### What is Chemotherapy?

Chemotherapy helps to control cancer cells by stopping them from growing and multiplying. However, this treatment not only destroys the cancer cells but can affect healthy cells, as well, causing side effects. After the treatments are finished, healthy cells usually repair themselves. When we use chemotherapy to treat cancer, we use different types of medications called “anti-cancer drugs.” Depending on the type of cancer, the extent of the disease, and your pet’s overall health, there are different drugs that may be prescribed.

### Pet Cancer Treatment Side Effects

We use many of the same drugs human oncologists do, but dogs do not generally suffer the same kind of side effects, such as hair loss, that human cancer patients may experience. Because chemotherapy in dogs is often used to assist in prolonging their lives, we are able to utilize lower doses and fewer drug combinations to treat them. However, there are some pets that may experience some adverse side effects such as:

  * Nausea

  * Vomiting

  * Fever or sepsis

Working with you, we’ll make sure you know what to expect and how to ease your pet’s discomfort. We can also advise you on the best foods to feed your pet if side effects are causing digestive problems.

### Pet Chemotherapy in Lincoln

Getting the news that your beloved fur baby has cancer can be devastating. In many, many cases, however, there is hope. Just like chemotherapy has helped countless human patients, it may be effective for your pet, too. To learn more about pet chemotherapy in Lincoln, Omaha, and the surrounding areas, contact Nebraska Animal Medical and Emergency Center today. Nebraska Animal Medical and Emergency Center offers pet chemotherapy in Lincoln, Omaha, and throughout Nebraska.

# Chemotherapy

Chemotherapy is available at Memorial Hospital Specialty Clinic. Memorial Health Care Systems (MHCS) has partnered with Cancer Partners of Nebraska to offer a local, more convenient location to receive select chemotherapy treatments. You may be able to avoid the commute to receive your chemotherapy. In collaboration with the doctors at Cancer Partners, MHCS can administer chemotherapy, biotherapy and hormone therapy. If you or someone you know could benefit from receiving chemotherapy closer to home and a support system, speak with Cancer Partners of Nebraska provider or call the Specialty Clinic at 402-646-4651.

MHCS Specialty Clinic nurses have completed the same required training and certification as Cancer Partners of Nebraska staff. MHCS Specialty Clinic Chemotherapy offers:

# Oncology

We know it can be difficult to discover that your pet has cancer. We’re here to help you every step of the way from diagnosis to treatment.

Image: Golden retriever dog laying down

### Overview

We know it can be extremely difficult to discover that your pet has cancer. We’re here to help you every step of the way from diagnosis to treatment.

We offer a range of treatment plans and tailor them to the needs of your pet in an effort to attack the disease they are fighting and maintain their lifestyle.

### Why would my pet need oncology treatments?

If your pet has been diagnosed with cancer, our team can help you decide on the best treatment plan. Depending on the specific type of cancer your pet has, treatment may include in the following (either stand alone or a combination of treatments):

>   * Radiation therapy

  * Chemotherapy

  * Nutrition/Diet

> ### When should my pet have oncology treatments?

We will determine the proper veterinary treatment schedule based off of your pet’s condition. If cancer spreads, chemotherapy may be recommended.

### How do you treat cancer in my pet?

Our goal is to provide maximum benefit with minimal effect on quality of life. Depending on the condition, we may recommend any of the following treatment options for your pet.

Radiation may be recommended in many different settings and can be a viable treatment for certain tumors and slow or prevent recurrences of many kinds of cancer. The different methods of radiation can help treat pain, inflammation, and rid cancer cells by using a beam of energy targeting the tumor region.

Chemotherapy uses a combination of drugs to kill cancer cells. The combination of drugs used will vary depending on the patient’s condition and are highly tailored to the specific needs of each patient. Chemotherapy drugs are injected either into the vein or under the skin and can only be administered at the practice.  

A carefully developed diet can help patients fight their condition and provide vital nutrients essential for recovery. A diet can be extremely beneficial for patients who are undergoing surgery, radiation, or chemotherapy.

It is important to understand that these treatment options do not necessarily cure your pet’s condition. Treatment options are performed to attack and fight off the effects of your pet’s condition so that they can maintain their quality of life. Many pets who undergo these treatment options have gained months, and sometimes even years of life.

## HOPE VETERINARY ONCOLOGY SERVICES IS PROUD TO BE AN INDEPENDENT PRACTICE.

## Remote Consulting Services

At Hope Veterinary Oncology Services, we bring cancer care right to your pet with our mobile in-person treatments, so you don’t have to travel far. We also offer remote consulting for pet owners, helping you understand your pet’s diagnosis and treatment options through a Zoom session. Our Cancer Care Plans even guide your local vet in providing care without the need for IV chemotherapy, making it easier to give your pet the best possible care.

## Our Remote Consulting Services

Every year in the United States, 8 million dogs and cats get cancer – but only 1 in 10 will get help from a veterinary oncologist. It’s a troubling thought, and we know how much you love your furry companion. You’re not alone in wanting to make sure they get the care they deserve.

The challenges of logistics and cost often keep pets from getting the help they need. That’s where we come in. At Hope Veterinary Oncology Services, we’re a small practice emotionally invested in making cancer care more accessible so your pet can get the treatment they need without added stress. Big corporate medicine can offer more technology, automation and a huge number of support staff. We at Hope offer personal, individualized, heartfelt care. You want the best for them, and so do we!

Here’s how we can help:

  * Every pet is unique and every cancer is different. That’s why at Hope we find great fulfillment in formulating individualized and integrative Cancer Care Plans that improve quality of life and maximize longevity for each patient whether they live in Washington or Nebraska. This means that we review each patient’s situation, diagnosis, special needs, diet and lifestyle, then formulate a plan that makes sense for that patient and her family. This may or may not include chemotherapy, but will always include strategies to help prolong an excellent QOL.
  * Mobile, in-person oncology care brings cancer treatment closer to your pet in western Washington.

# Oncology

Our team works closely with oncologists across the state of Nebraska to be able to provide at-home, local treatments. This allows our patients to still get expert care while staying close to home during treatments. This provides comfort instead of long travel times. We are also honored to partner with oncologists who see patients at our specialty clinic and then are able to have continued care at our infusion center if needed.

At our Chemotherapy Outpatient Infusion Center, patients arrive carrying uncertainty, and we hope that they leave knowing they are not alone. Every patient is treated with respect, compassion, and attention. O ur dedicated team works diligently to ensure they are always the priority. 

 

Our oncology team consists of certified RNs, Philip Miller and Ainsley Rickertson, as well as Dr Jordan Sieh DNP and Dr. Johnna Richter  PharmD who all significantly contribute to ensuring treatments are delivered safely, accurately, and individualized to each patients specialized treatment plan. 

 

We know that no two patients are the same ,and in collaboration with oncologists, we provide eduction to patients and families about treatment plans, side effects, and questions that arise along their journey.

Proud to partner with the Cancer Partners of Nebraska and Callahan Cancer Center.

# Chemotherapy

Nebraska Hematology-Oncology (NHO) offers cancer patients chemotherapy treatments within the comfort and convenience of the NHO clinic. Our outpatient treatment center is designed for patient comfort and convenience while providing the most advanced cancer and hematology care possible.
Over 90% of our patients’ chemotherapy treatments are provided right here. This avoids the inconvenience of trips to the hospital and provides you with easy access to your physician if you have any questions. Our state-of-the-art facility provides the most advanced treatment protocols available in a safe, clean, comfortable environment.
We offer a spacious chemotherapy infusion suite complete with audio-visual entertainment for each station and a library with resource books, support group information, and light reading material. A computer with Internet access is also available to patients and families.
Our lab is on-site for patient convenience and immediate test results.
Patients find outpatient treatment at our clinic to be less stressful because the treatment setting is stable. Your medical team, including our highly trained oncology nurses, seldom changes. Patients find comfort in dealing with people they’ve come to know and trust.
When your care requires radiation therapy, surgery, or other treatment that we do not provide at our clinic, our doctors and staff will coordinate your care with the appropriate providers. We are a well-established part of Nebraska’s cancer treatment network and we will make sure each patient gets the treatment needed at the appropriate time and from the appropriate source.
We continue to strive for improved patient care and your comments are important to us. Please tell us how we can better meet your needs.

(x) Post-surgical and mechanical disorders. 
 
005.243  CHEMOTHERAPY. Nebraska Medicaid covers chemotherapy which has been 
provided and billed in accordance with this chapter. 
 
005.254  IMMUNIZATIONS. Nebraska Medicaid covers routine immunizations for children, 
adolescent, and adults that are medically necessary according to the Advisory Committee on 
Immunization Practices’ guidelines that are effective the date the service is provided.  
Immunizations are available to children and adolescents from birth through age 20 under the 
Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) program. Vaccines for 
those individuals age 18 and younger are available through the Vaccine for Children (VFC) 
program. The Department will not reimburse for a physician’s private stock vaccine when the 
vaccine is available through the Vaccine for Children (VFC) program.
